The development team wants to ensure the reliability of their application by monitoring its external dependencies, such as third-party payment gateways and database services. Which approach should they take to effectively implement dependency telemetry according to the AWS Well-Architected Framework?

B. Implement Amazon Route 53 health checks for all external dependencies and use AWS CloudTrail to log API calls.
C. Set up Amazon CloudWatch Metrics and Alarms for monitoring the performance and availability of third-party services and databases.
D. Deploy an on-premises load balancer in front of the e-commerce application to route traffic and monitor health.

Option B is inadequate as Route 53 health checks can only monitor DNS-level availability and do not provide detailed metrics on the service's performance. AWS CloudTrail logs API calls but does not offer real-time performance insights, making it unsuitable for dependency telemetry. Option D is inappropriate because deploying an on-premises load balancer would be a significant over-engineering effort that introduces complexity without providing the necessary monitoring capabilities.
